title: Setu Invoice Generator vs Vyapar: Which Free Billing Tool Actually Stays Free in 2026?
seoTitle: Setu Invoice Generator vs Vyapar (2026) — Honest Comparison
metaDescription: Vyapar's Android app is free but desktop billing is a yearly licence. Setu's Invoice Generator runs free in any browser. An honest 2026 comparison.
excerpt: Vyapar's Android app is free for life, but desktop billing is a yearly licence and the features most shops grow into sit behind it. Setu's Invoice Generator is a browser tool with no account at all. Here's which trade actually fits your shop.

faq.question: Is Setu's Invoice Generator really free, with no invoice limit?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no plan and no cap on how many invoices you generate. It stays free because it does not carry a server cost — the PDF is built in your browser.

faq.question: Is Vyapar's free version enough for a small shop?
faq.answer: Often, yes, if you bill from a single Android phone and don't need multi-user access or the desktop build. The paid licence starts to matter when you add a second user, a Windows counter machine, or the deeper inventory features.

faq.question: Can I move my invoice history from Vyapar to something else?
faq.answer: Vyapar supports exports and backups, and you should test that export before you need it. Confirm you can get parties, items and transaction history out in CSV or Excel — not just a proprietary backup file only Vyapar can read.

faq.question: Does Setu's Invoice Generator file my GST returns?
faq.answer: No. It formats a compliant-looking tax invoice and does the GST arithmetic, but filing GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B is separate. If you'd rather not do it yourself, that's what our accounting and bookkeeping service is for.

faq.question: What if I need billing plus stock plus reports?
faq.answer: Then you've outgrown both a browser tool and, arguably, a standalone invoicing app. Look at Setu Retail or the browser-based POS — billing, stock and a profit dashboard in one place.

bodyHtml:
Ask ten Indian shopkeepers what they bill with and a good number will say Vyapar. It earned that position honestly — it was one of the first apps to put a proper GST invoice on an Android phone, and for a lot of businesses it replaced a duplicate book and a calculator in one go.

But "free" does a lot of work in that sentence. Vyapar is free the way a lot of Indian SaaS is free: the mobile app is free for life, the desktop version is a paid yearly licence, and several of the features people actually end up needing sit behind the licence. That is a perfectly reasonable business model. It just isn't the same thing as free.

Setu's Invoice Generator sits at the other end of that spectrum. It is a browser tool, it has no account, no licence, and no plan to upgrade to — because there is nothing to sell you. What it gives up in exchange is everything a database gives you: history, stock, reports, sync.

This post is about which of those two trades makes sense for your shop in 2026.

How Vyapar's model works

Vyapar is a full billing-and-accounting product. You install it, you create a company file, and from then on it holds your data: parties, items, stock, payments, and every invoice you have ever raised. That is genuinely useful, and it is why people stay.

The pricing, as publicly listed in August 2026, runs roughly like this — check vyaparapp.in for the current numbers before you plan a budget:

  • Mobile-only licences in the ₹699–₹799 per year range
  • Desktop licences in the ₹3,799–₹4,099 per year range
  • Mobile + desktop combo licences in the ₹4,399–₹4,799 per year range
  • Segment editions (Retail Pro, Distributor Pro, Manufacturing Pro) priced separately
  • A free trial on the desktop/premium features, and a free-for-life Android app

The Android app being free for life is real and it matters. The catch is what "premium" covers: multi-user access with role-based access, desktop use, some print and report options, and the deeper inventory features. If your billing lives on one phone and you never need a second user, you may never pay. If you grow a counter, a back office and a second outlet, you will.

The second thing to understand is where the data lives. Vyapar stores your company file on the device (with backup and sync options), which is fine — until you want it somewhere else. That is a vendor lock-in question worth asking of any billing app, and it is the same question we raised in Setu Customer Ledger vs Khatabook.

How Setu's Invoice Generator works instead

Setu's Invoice Generator is deliberately smaller. You open the page, fill in your business details and the client's, add line items, and download a PDF. There is no signup and no company file.

Specifically, it does:

  • Automatic GST maths with a CGST/SGST split, and multiple tax rates per line item
  • GSTIN validation and amount-in-words in the lakh/crore format Indian buyers expect
  • Three invoice templates plus your own brand colour
  • A UPI ID and payment terms block on the invoice itself
  • Instant PDF download, generated on your device

And on privacy, the page is blunt about it: PDF generation happens in your browser, and your invoice data never reaches Setu's servers. The tool auto-saves your details into browser storage so the next invoice is faster — which also means clearing your browser clears your details.

It is also explicit about what it is not: a formatting and calculation tool, not a return-filing or compliance product. It will not file GSTR-1 for you.

If you need a quote before the invoice, the Quotation Generator works the same way. If you need to record who owes you what, the Customer Ledger does that separately.

Where Vyapar genuinely wins

Be honest about this before you switch anything.

You need history. A browser tool that forgets is useless if a customer calls about invoice #217 from March. Vyapar keeps every invoice, every party and every payment, and lets you search them.

You sell from stock. If billing an item must reduce inventory, trigger a reorder point and feed a stock take, you need a database. A PDF generator cannot do this and should not pretend to.

You have staff. Two people billing at a counter, one person doing purchases, an owner who wants to see it all — that's a multi-user product, and that's a paid tier.

You want accounts receivable chased for you. Automated payment reminders against outstanding invoices are a real feature with real cash-flow value, and Vyapar has them.

You are already three years of data deep. Migration cost is a genuine reason to stay. Just make sure you can export.

Where the free browser tool wins

You bill occasionally. Consultants, freelancers, contractors, service businesses raising eight invoices a month. A ₹4,000/year licence for eight PDFs is not a good trade.

You are on a Mac, an iPhone, or a shared machine. Vyapar's desktop build is Windows. A browser tool doesn't care.

You want the invoice to look like yours, today. Three templates, your brand colour, a PDF in about four minutes, no install and no trial countdown.

You are testing a new business. Before you know whether the business exists, buying a yearly licence is premature. Start free, migrate when the volume justifies it.

Your data policy is "nowhere". For a lot of small firms, "the invoice never leaves my laptop" is a feature, not a limitation.

What a month of actual use looks like

Picture a two-person interior design studio in Pune. Six to ten invoices a month, each with a couple of line items at 18% GST, paid by NEFT or UPI. Some months they raise a quotation first.

With Setu, their month is: open the Invoice Generator, the browser has remembered their business block and GSTIN, fill in the client, two lines, download, email. Roughly three minutes an invoice. Payments get logged in the Cash Book, receivables sit in the Customer Ledger, and at year end they hand their CA a folder of PDFs and a CSV. Total software spend: zero.

Now picture a hardware store in Nashik. Two hundred bills a month, 900 SKUs, two staff at the counter, credit customers, and a supplier ledger. With Setu's free tools they'd be stitching together an Invoice Generator, a Stock Register and a Customer Ledger by hand, and they'd feel the seams by week two. That shop should be on a proper billing database — Vyapar, or a POS like Setu Retail if they want billing and stock in one place.

Same country, same GST, completely different answer.

The honest bottom line

Vyapar is not overpriced. For a shop that bills all day, a desktop licence at around ₹3,800 a year is about ₹10 a day, and it replaces work. The mistake is paying for a database when what you needed was a nicely formatted PDF.

So use the volume test. Under roughly 25 invoices a month with no stock to track, the free browser tool is enough and you should stop shopping. Over that, or the moment stock and staff enter the picture, buy the licence — or move to a POS that does billing, stock and reporting together instead of paying for two things.

Either way, ask both vendors the same question before you commit: can I export everything, in a format someone else can read, on the day I decide to leave? That is the only lock-in question that matters.

Try it first: the Invoice Generator needs no signup — raise one real invoice on it today and see whether the gap is a dealbreaker or a non-issue.
